issues.failure_explanation: A batch contains the vectors indexed from $\undertilde n$ through $\widetilde n$, so adjoining all of them to $V_{\undertilde n}$ produces the space after $b$ additions, namely $V_{\widetilde n+1}$. As written, the first iteration overwrites $V_{b-1}$ and never defines $V_b$, although the next iteration requires $V_b$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the assignment and orthogonalization index by $V_{\widetilde n+1}$, consistently interpreting it as the span after the batch.
issues.overall_effect: The stated procedure cannot proceed to its second batch, and the spaces and errors used throughout the convergence analysis are not generated by the displayed algorithm.
issues.title: Batch algorithm stores the new space under the wrong index
issues.why_classification: The index correction is forced and local and preserves the intended procedure and all advertised guarantees, subject to the paper's other defects.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For our analysis in Section \ref{Sec:Analysis} below, we actually do not need to fix how the remaining $b-1$ elements are chosen 
 as long as the first one is chosen according to line \ref{line:eq:batchfirst}.

issues.failure_explanation: Nothing in the batch selection implies that an interior vector retains residual at least as large as the maximum residual after the completed batch. Even with the exact initial-distance surrogate, take $b=2$ in $\mathbb R^3$ with $f_0=e_1$, an initially unit-norm $f_1$ arbitrarily close to $e_1$, and another element $ce_3$ with the closeness residual smaller than $c<1$. The batch may select $f_0,f_1$, while after their addition the residual of $ce_3$ is $c$ and $|a_{1,1}|<c=\sigma_2$, contradicting (P1). Arbitrary choices of the remaining vectors make the failure still more immediate. The same invalid inference occurs in the Banach-space lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose and realize a batch-selection invariant that controls each new vector's residual relative to the error after the batch, and then rebuild the convergence argument for that invariant.
issues.overall_effect: The determinant/product estimates underlying every Hilbert- and Banach-space convergence rate lose their required diagonal lower bound, so the paper's main batch-greedy rates are unproved.
issues.title: Interior batch vectors need not satisfy the diagonal lower bound
issues.why_classification: The false lower bound is the central input to both convergence analyses, and repairing it requires a materially different batch-selection guarantee or new proof architecture rather than a local calculation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the infimum in the definition of $d_n$ is attained, the corresponding argument $X_n$ is called \emph{optimal in the sense of Kolmogorov}.
Let $X_m$ be an $m$-dimensional optimal subspace of $X$ in the sense of Kolmogorov, i.e., $\dist(\cF,X_m)=d_m$, $m=1,\ldots, K$.

issues.failure_explanation: The source itself only defines an optimal subspace conditionally on attainment, but neither theorem assumes attainment or proves it for the stated arbitrary compact subset of an arbitrary Hilbert or Banach space. The proofs therefore invoke an object not supplied by their hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Let $X_m$ be an $m$-dimensional optimal subspace of $X$ in the sense of Kolmogorov, i.e., $\dist(\cF,X_m)=d_m$, $m=1,\ldots, K$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $m$-dimensional subspaces whose errors are at most $d_m+\varepsilon$ throughout both proofs and pass to the limit as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
issues.overall_effect: The product estimates and all results derived from them have a gap for cases in which the width infimum is not attained.
issues.title: Kolmogorov-optimal subspaces are assumed without attainment
issues.why_classification: An epsilon-minimizer argument is a standard local replacement that preserves the statements and constants without new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the $2n$-th root in the proof yields exponent $(n-m)/n$, not $(n-m)/m$. The displayed statement is generally much stronger when $m<n$ and is not established by the argument.
issues.overall_effect: Part (i)'s general minimum estimate is unsupported, although its separately stated special case with exponent $1/2$ agrees with the exponent produced by the proof.
issues.title: General Hilbert estimate has the wrong exponent
issues.why_classification: The correction is syntactically local but materially weakens an explicit quantitative bound, so it withdraws mathematical content rather than merely repairing notation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By using $\sigma_{2s} \leq C_1 (2s)^{-\alpha}$ and $d_s \leq C_0 s^{-\alpha}$ we get

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed constants and exponents depend on the index $n$ and improve as $n$ grows. At a first failure $M$, the induction hypothesis only gives the earlier bound with $C_1(2s,b)$, not with the smaller quantity $C_1(M,b)$ that the proof denotes by the same symbol. The same problem occurs for the index-dependent exponential constants and in the Banach-space induction. Thus the displayed contradictions do not establish the sharpened pointwise constants.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that the statement in (ii) does not hold and let $M$ be the first value where $\sigma_M(\cF)>C_1M^{-\alpha}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the varying quantities in the induction by uniform worst-case constants, as suggested by the subsequent Hilbert-space reformulation, or supply a new induction that explicitly compares the constants at all earlier indices.
issues.overall_effect: The $n$-dependent refinements in parts (ii) and (iii) of both convergence theorems are unsupported; consequences using those particular constants are likewise unreliable.
issues.title: Minimal-counterexample proofs treat index-dependent constants as fixed
issues.why_classification: A source-supported repair preserves the qualitative polynomial and exponential rates but loses the advertised sharper index-dependent constants or requires a contained new induction.

issues.failure_explanation: For $n\ge b\ge2$, the first entries of the two minima have the stated ratio, but the theorem defines each $c_1$ as the minimum with a second entry. Those second entries can be active and have ratio $b^{-\alpha}$ rather than $(2/3)^\alpha$. The proof simply discards them without a hypothesis ensuring that the first entries attain both minima.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add conditions guaranteeing that the first term realizes both minima, or withdraw the equality and state only a comparison that accounts for both minimum terms.
issues.overall_effect: The exact universal factor claimed for the asymptotic loss, and the prose interpretation based on it, do not follow under the corollary's hypotheses.
issues.title: Corollary ignores the minima defining the exponential constants
issues.why_classification: Repair requires restricting the corollary's parameter regime or materially weakening its quantitative conclusion, but not rebuilding the full convergence theory.

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficient on the penultimate expression is $2\sqrt{C_0}\,\gamma^{-1}$, whereas the theorem defines $C_1=\sqrt{2C_0}\,\gamma^{-1}$. The asserted equality loses a factor $\sqrt2$, so the proof does not establish the stated prefactor.

failure_location.quote: \sigma_{2s\hue{+b-1}} \leq 2 \gamma^{-1} \sqrt{sd_s} \leq 2 \gamma^{-1} \sqrt{s \ C_0 e^{-c_0 s^\alpha}} = C_1 \sqrt{s} \ e^{- \frac{1}{2}c_0 s^\alpha}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase $C_1$ to $2\sqrt{C_0}\,\gamma^{-1}$ and update the occurrence of $\ln(C_1\sqrt b)$ accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Part (iii)'s explicit Banach-space exponential bound, including the logarithmic term built from its $C_1$, is not justified with the stated constant.
issues.title: Banach exponential estimate uses an insufficient prefactor
issues.why_classification: A direct local enlargement of the prefactor repairs this calculation without changing the rate, regime, or proof structure.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing $A=\lceil2+(b-1)/s\rceil$, the assumed range gives $As+q<As+A\le2As$, not $As+q\ge2As$. Consequently the first comparison in Case 2 is based on the wrong ordering. In Case 3, $M\le b$ does not imply $\sqrt M e^{-c_1M^\alpha}\ge\sqrt b e^{-c_1b^\alpha}$ without a monotonicity argument, and such monotonicity is not guaranteed for this product.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide corrected estimates for $As<M<As+A$ that handle the square-root factor, and separately choose or prove a uniform constant controlling all indices $1\le M\le b$.
issues.overall_effect: Even after correcting the prefactor, the induction does not cover the intermediate and initial indices, so the Banach-space exponential estimate remains unproved.
issues.title: Banach exponential proof uses reversed interval and base-case inequalities
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained but nontrivial reconstruction of two cases of the induction; it need not change the qualitative exponential rate but is more than routine algebra.
